audit_findings.title: Rhode earnout liability appears absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.829 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.323 per diluted share and 4.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A contingent cash claim should be deducted in the equity bridge unless expected payments are already modeled in OE; the noncash fair-value remeasurements should not substitute for the liability.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026, the contingent consideration was remeasured to $ 64.7 million, driven by the outperformance of rhode's revenue results for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, and a revised upward forecast for the remainder of the performance periods.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the latest filed liability is $80.829 million, while the bridge contains no contingent-consideration deduction. Deducting it would reduce bear, base and bull values to approximately $22.20, $29.28 and $33.76 per share, respectively, and base buy-below to about $20.49. The market price of $109.67 remains more than three times the adjusted bull value, so the omission does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with an $80.829 million deduction and reconcile the $57.649 million FY2026 and $16.080 million FY2027 remeasurement addbacks against any explicitly modeled earnout payments.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial year of rhode against the full post-acquisition capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed pro forma FY2026 net income was $30.054 million versus $26.318 million actual, a computed $3.736 million difference, but no pro forma OE was provided
audit_findings.mechanism: The mixed-period anchor omits pre-acquisition rhode cash generation while also omitting part of the annual acquisition financing cost and related working-capital and capital requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: Since the rhode Acquisition date, the results of operations for rhode of $ 293.5 million of net sales and $ 112.8 million of net income for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, have been included within the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year perimeter is demonstrated, but its OE effect is unresolved. The small $3.736 million pro forma net-income difference does not establish the owner-earnings effect because net income does not reconcile rhode working capital, maintenance investment, noncash acquisition accounting or the timing of interest. The record therefore cannot establish whether the mixed-period anchor materially understates or overstates sustainable OE.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an April 1, 2025 pro forma OE reconciliation incorporating pre-acquisition rhode operating cash generation, maintenance investment and working capital, full-year interest, intangible-amortization treatment, earnout treatment and the acquisition shares; compare it with the $108.5 million anchor without replacing the approved input.

audit_findings.title: A one-time $47.1 million acquisition cash payment may have been embedded in recurring OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.1 million, equal to 43.4% of anchor OE; a full anchor reversal computes to approximately +$7.76, +$10.83 and +$12.79 per share in bear, base and bull cases
audit_findings.mechanism: If the acquisition-specific cash payment reduced the CFO-based anchor, the DCF perpetuates it as an annual operating cost even though it belongs once in acquisition economics.
audit_findings.evidence: This included net income, before deducting depreciation, amortization and other non-cash items of $262.0 million, partially offset by acquisition-related seller expenses of $47.1 million in connection with the rhode Acquisition, and an increase in working capital of $2.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $47.1 million cash payment, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the OE workpaper retained it. Even under the conservative sensitivity that the entire amount is reversed from recurring OE, bear, base and bull values rise only to approximately $31.28, $41.43 and $47.87 per share, with base buy-below near $29.00. Those values remain far below the $109.67 market price, so this possibility cannot change the current valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $47.1 million cash-flow adjustment into the OE workpaper and document that it is recognized exactly once; if embedded in anchor OE, rerun the disclosed sensitivity without changing the approved valuation inputs.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 OE may contain a nonrecurring tariff burden subject to refund
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.5 million paid in FY2026; by June 30, 2026, $51.1 million had been refunded, including $50.1 million credited to cost of sales and $1.0 million to inventory; reversing the full $58.5 million from the anchor computes to at most approximately +$9.64, +$13.45 and +$15.88 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical tariff costs may depress anchor OE, while refunds increase cash and later earnings; replacement tariffs remain a recurring margin cost that must not be removed from projected OE without support.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year 2026, the Company paid approximately $ 58.5 million of IEEPA Tariffs.
audit_findings.explanation: The refund is no longer merely hypothetical: $51.1 million was received and the latest cash bridge includes the resulting cash. The exact sustainable OE normalization remains mixed because replacement tariffs of 10% to 12.5% were imposed. Even an unsupported upper-bound sensitivity reversing all $58.5 million would raise the bull value only to about $50.96 per share and base buy-below to about $30.84, still far below the $109.67 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2026 tariff amounts between cost of sales, inventory and OE; exclude the $50.1 million refund from recurring OE, confirm it is captured only through cash, and document the recurring replacement-tariff assumption used in each scenario.

audit_findings.title: Unhedged RMB exposure is large relative to anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.0 million annual net-income and cost-of-sales sensitivity for a 10% adverse RMB movement, equal to 47.0% of the $108.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A sustained adverse RMB movement would compress gross margin and OE, potentially lowering the starting earnings base and achievable growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on a hypothetical 10% adverse movement in RMB as compared to the US dollar, our cost of sales and net income would be adversely affected by approximately $51.0 million for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a filed hypothetical sensitivity, not a demonstrated currency loss or error in current OE. Its scale is large enough to matter if an adverse movement occurs and persists, but the record does not show that such a movement is presently embedded outside the scenarios. It is therefore a forward-looking exposure to monitor rather than a current valuation correction.
audit_findings.action: At each filing, compare actual RMB movements and sourcing terms with the disclosed sensitivity; rerun a sustained currency-stress case if pricing, supplier negotiations or sourcing changes do not offset the exposure.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified litigation claims are not represented in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured settlement, judgment or defense-related cash obligation would reduce OE or become a liability deducted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company can provide no assurance as to the scope and outcome of these matters and cannot reasonably estimate any loss or range of loss, if any, that may arise from these matters.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuits are existing proceedings, but no probable loss, accrual or estimable range has been filed. The record therefore establishes a contingent possibility, not a demonstrated omitted liability, and cannot show whether the amount could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings and court developments for class certification, settlement discussions, insurance limits and deductibles, accruals or an estimable loss range; rerun the bridge only when a supportable company-level cash exposure is available.
